messages:
maya: Heads-up — experimenting with a "deferential degrade" rollout option for automatic fallback. Instead of an immediate model swap, we gradually step down capabilities (eg. full model -> quantized variant -> cached prefix -> canned short answer). want quick UX + API design feedback.
jon: interesting. what's the main trigger surface? latency spikes only or errors + quality signals too?
maya: both. priority is latency and downstream 5xx, but also a soft quality signal (confidence/hallucination indicator). we should expose trigger types: latency_ms, error_rate, quality_score.
priya: console POV: show current active tier, the reason for last transition, and a small timeline so ops can see the staircase. also expose "why did we degrade" explainer with link to traces.
sam: agree. ops needs one-click rollback and an ability to set a max-degrade-level per rollout. 
maya: good call. sketch of rollout config I'm thinking: 
```yaml
rollout:
  id: r-123
  degrade_policy:
    strategy: deferential
    tiers:
      - name: full
        model: gptx-8k
      - name: quantized
        model: gptx-8k-q4
      - name: prefix_cached
        cache: prefix_kv
      - name: canned
        response_template: low_confidence_template
    triggers:
      latency_ms: 1200
      error_rate: 0.02
      quality_score: 0.6
    hysteresis_ms: 30000
    sample_for_audit: 0.05
```
jon: love the structure. a few questions: hysteresis_ms default and sample_for_audit meaning?
maya: hysteresis_ms = minimum time before re-escalating back up. sample_for_audit = fraction of degraded requests we snapshot for human review + evals.
priya: audit UX: sampled items should include the prompt, full response path (what tier produced it), the why-reason code, and a link to replay. retention policy needs to default to 30 days but configurable. privacy note: strip PII if tenant opts-in.
sam: alerting: escalate when we hit tier 3+ for 5m across multiple regions. also surface cost delta when we step down (we save but may change quality).
maya: console indicator ideas: small badge next to rollout name: orange/yellow gradient for partial degrade, red for full canned. hover shows reason code and last 3 events. timeline mini-graph shows token throughput and error spikes.
jon: API contract: how do callers see that a request was degraded? Add fields to the response envelope: `x-redwood-degrade-tier`, `x-redwood-degrade-reason`, `x-redwood-degrade-sampled`?
priya: yes but keep header names consistent. I suggest returning JSON fields in the envelope for apps that depend on content: `degraded: true/false`, `degrade_tier: "quantized"`, `degrade_reason: "latency:1500ms"`, `degrade_trace_id: "t-..."`, `audit_sampled: true/false`. That way apps can show fallback banners.
sam: also provide a hook: when degraded and audit_sampled==true, post to an internal review queue (or pubsub) with context so SRE/ML can triage.
maya: good. opsbot: what about operator overrides? we need a way to manually pin a tier or force-disable automatic degrade for a rollout.
opsbot: opsbot: +1; propose two quick actions in UI: "pin tier" (with comment) and "suspend auto-degrade" (with TTL). actions emit an audit event with user, comment, and trace.
jon: edgecases: what if degrade to quantized reduces latency but increases hallucination — we'll need a quality regression detection and auto-rollback to previous tier or fail-open?
priya: we should run a tiny post-degrade eval set (lightweight prompts) to detect regressions. if quality_score drops below threshold for X samples, send an urgent operator notification and optionally promote rollback.
sam: telemetry: include metrics per-tier: p95 latency, error_rate, quality_score, tokens_per_request, cost_per_token. make them queryable by timeframe and exportable to dashboards.
maya: UI mock: rollout detail page with left column: live tier & actions, middle: timeline + metrics per tier, right: recent degrade events + sampled request list. each sampled request expands with prompt + full outputs for each tier (if available).
jon: one more API note: keep compatibility — default response should not break existing clients. make new degrade fields optional and behind a response-version header until GA.
priya: audit retention + compliance: add per-tenant toggle to disable request body capture for sampled audits; in that case keep only metadata and diffs. default: capture full for 30d.
sam: question about rollout testing: provide a "dry-run" mode that simulates degrade transitions (no actual switch) but still records events so console can show how it would have behaved. helps PMs and SREs validate thresholds.
maya: yes — add `mode: active | dry_run` to the rollout API. dry_run emits all the same logs + simulated transitions but doesn't change runtime routing.
jon: perf: ensure prefix cache tier doesn't leak KV contexts across tenants — stronger isolation required.
maya: noted. also need to document operator mental model: degrade is reversible, conservative by default, and auditable. keep UI affordances minimal at first.
priya: can we add a small "reason vocabulary" codes (latency_spike, error_surge, quality_drop, manual_pin) so downstream tooling can filter?
maya: yes. standardize codes and map to human-friendly strings in UI.
sam: final ask: add cost/quality tradeoff estimates per tier in the console so PMs can decide acceptable thresholds. even rough % estimates help.
maya: agreed. next steps: I'll spin up a proto of the rollout JSON + console mock and post a dry_run sample for folks to play with. if no blockers, we can propose API fields for review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
jon: :thumbsup:
priya: looking forward to the mock.
opsbot: Note: created task INF-8421 to track prototyping + privacy review.
